sentences.text:
Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent [
 Order

This appeal by the appellant/claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 05.04.2024 passed by Additional Member, MACT, Khaargone District Mandleshwar in Claim Case No.132/2023.
2.
The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability is not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in dispute.

As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of injured claimant, who suffered fracture of 2nd to 6th ribs, due to which the injured is suffering for lifetime permanent disability, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.72,400/-along with interest.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:12071 2 MA-8055-2024 in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

It is further submitted that the learned tribunal has not specifically considered with regard to quantum of compensation for permanent disability and only Rs.72,400/- is awarded,
which is not just and proper.
It is also submitted that in absence of permanent disability certificate and examination of doctor, the amount should be on higher side.
It is also submitted that the injured has suffered fracture in his 2nd to 6th ribs and he has faced the pain for long time and as well as income loss including the loss of estate also.
Therefore, the learned tribunal was not justified Jagdishchandra Gupta vs Sumit on 6 May, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31416153/
1 in granted the amount of award to the tune of Rs.72,400/- Hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the matter.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contends that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the amount of compensation in the matter which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, more particularly the age of the claimant, nature of injuries, loss of income and loss of estate in the considered opinion of this Court, the amount of compensation deserves to be enhanced to some extent considering the sonography report attached with the record and other documents, this Court is of the view that the amount awarded by learned tribunal should be enhanced to the extent of Rs.45,000/-, therefore, the claimant is entitled to get total amount of award as Rs.72,400+45,000/-=1,17,400/-.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12071 3 MA-8055-2024 6 .
Thus, the appellant/claimant is entitled to an additional sum of (Rs.1,17,400-72,400) = Rs.45,000/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
7. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The claimants are entitled to get total amount of compensation i.e. Rs.1,17,400/-.
The enhanced amount i.e. Rs.45,000/- shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three month s from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

8. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
9. In view of above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants- claimants stands disposed of.
With the aforesaid, appeal stands disposed off.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE amit Jagdishchandra Gupta vs Sumit on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31416153/
